card.title: HOME GUARD
card.text: Deal 2 damage to target unit. Add a GARRISON to your hand.
card.flavorText: Formed in May 1940 as the Local Defence Volunteers, the Home Guard quickly became a vital part of Britain's defensive strategy during WWII. It was made up of over 1.5 million men who were too old, too young or medically unfit for regular service, as well as those in reserved occupations (exempt from military service). Their main task was to resist a German invasion by delaying enemy forces long enough for the regular army to respond. Volunteers were initially given only armbands marked "LDV" and received little equipment. Many units improvised weapons or used donated civilian firearms. Eventually, they were issued standard rifles and uniforms. The Home Guard guarded factories, bridges and airfields and manned roadblocks and observation posts. During the Blitz, they were also tasked with guarding unexploded bombs, a role that cost over 1,000 lives. By 1942, the Home Guard took over some coastal artillery and anti-aircraft duties, freeing up regular troops for overseas deployment. Although unpaid, the service attracted widespread support, with entire platoons formed from workplaces or social clubs. The Home Guard represented a massive volunteer effort to protect Britain from within. It officially stood down in late 1944 and was disbanded a year later.
